comments.body:
Pre-sweep against origin/main 7927904a0 and tickets-branch 0b9294311b5. This plan's central number was stale in a way that would have inverted the epic's conclusion, so the Context, Approach, Scope, Testing and all acceptance criteria were rewritten. The title no longer pins a pair count, so it cannot go stale the same way again.

What was wrong. The plan said '51 known duplicate pairs identified in ticket eac3, of which 44 are semantic', and AC1 required benchmark.json to hold 51 pairs. eac3 did measure 51, honestly and by this exact method, but it measured 2,679 tickets and 43 recorded duplicates links. Running the plan's own stated procedure today over 5,663 live tickets finds 482 links closing into 148 clusters over 630 tickets, enumerating to 1,524 pairs. AC1 was therefore unsatisfiable by its own Approach: no implementation could follow 'exactly as eac3 did' and arrive at 51. Counting both archived and live tickets gives the same 1,524, so archiving does not explain the gap.

What the re-measurement found that matters more than the count. 1,431 of the 1,524 pairs -- 94 percent -- have byte-identical normalized titles. They sit in 84 clusters that are each a single repeated title; the largest is 12 copies of one bridge-state rotation ticket and the next is 9 copies of one comment-triage ticket. Those are bulk-creation artifacts, almost certainly a retry loop, not independently authored duplicates. Normalized-title matching scores about 100 percent recall on them. A benchmark that pooled all 1,524 pairs would therefore have reported near-perfect recall for the cheapest lexical candidate and rejected vector search -- on an artifact. That is the precise opposite of eac3's finding, which was that the duplicates worth catching are semantic: it measured 14 percent lexical recall because 44 of its 51 were semantic.

93 pairs have differing titles. That is the real benchmark, it is double eac3's 44, and it is the same kind of set. Spot-checked samples confirm the character: 'Attested snapshot fetch pulls unrelated oversized tickets branch' against 'Attested ref materialization broad-fetches all origin heads'; 'rebar doctor command' against 'rebar doctor: diagnose-and-heal health command'.

The rewrite keeps the story's intent -- choose a retrieval architecture on measurement -- and makes it measurable: the fixture stratifies every pair as lexical or semantic, recall is reported per stratum and never pooled, the semantic stratum is the decision criterion, and the lexical stratum is a control every candidate should near-saturate. The fixture records the tickets-branch SHA it was derived at, and --check re-derives the set at that SHA and refuses a fixture whose SHA is not an ancestor of current HEAD, so this specific staleness is now caught by the runner instead of by a reviewer.

Three further corrections, each measured rather than assumed:
- Scope said the top-level evals/ tree is created by the eval-harness epic's corpus-move story and that this story depends on it. That dependency has landed: evals/ was created by commit 91d39fd6061, 'Move research corpus out of docs to evals/'. Restated as completed work.
- Candidate 2 pointed at the retired ticket_digest prompt via 'the commit before its removal, recorded on the closing comment of the removal story under epic bossy-skittish-foal' -- an indirection through a comment that may or may not carry the SHA. Measured directly: the prompt was deleted by 2de5f341ec4, so it is readable at parent f147e08242f, where it lives in src/rebar/llm/contracts.py and src/rebar/llm/overlap/. The SHA is now named in the plan.
- Candidate 3 said boto3 is provided by the bedrock extra. The extra is pydantic-ai-slim[bedrock], which pulls boto3 transitively; boto3 1.43.68 imports in the worktree venv. Reworded to state the actual path rather than imply a direct dependency.

Verified correct and left alone: rebar list --full exists and is accepted; rebar.toml carries [llm] bedrock_region_name = us-east-1 at :213; scripts/check_adr_numbers.py and scripts/gen_adr_index.py both exist; docs/ticket-model.md documents the duplicates relation at :136 and :143. This ticket has no blockers, so it is reviewable now.

Bedrock embedding entitlement — measured, and it splits in two.

The epic's certified round-4 finding recorded that `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` scopes `bedrock:InvokeModel` to `anthropic.claude-*` only, with no embedding ARN, and concluded candidate 3 may have to be recorded `unavailable`. Measuring it shows the constraint is real but narrower than that, and candidate 3 IS measurable.

Measured from the operator identity that runs the eval harness
(`arn:aws:iam::896586841071:user/joe_frontier`), region `us-west-2`:

- `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` — OK, dim 1024
- `amazon.titan-embed-text-v1` — OK, dim 1536
- `cohere.embed-english-v3` — OK, dim 1024

Confirmed the policy text at `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf:64-66`; its resource list is exactly:

    arn:aws:bedrock:*::foundation-model/anthropic.claude-*
    arn:aws:bedrock:*:<acct>:inference-profile/*.anthropic.claude-*

So both statements hold, about different principals:

1. The **eval harness** runs under an operator identity and CAN call Titan. Candidate 3 is measurable, so AC2's "all three candidates" is satisfiable without an `unavailable` row.
2. The **review-bot instance role** (`rebar-gerrit-instance-role`) is scoped to Anthropic Claude and CANNOT call an embedding model. Adopting a vector architecture requires adding an embedding ARN to `iam_s7.tf`.

That second point is a deployment precondition, and the ADR will record it as one rather than as a measurement gap.

Scope note on the evidence: `iam_s7.tf:30-38` explicitly warns that entitlement must be re-verified from the instance and "never from an operator identity holding bedrock:*" — which is exactly what the test above used. It is therefore evidence about the eval path only. It does not show the instance role can call Titan, and I am not claiming it does; the instance-role scoping above comes from reading the policy, not from simulation.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
Empty digests driven to **0 of 630**. The rate went 27 → 4 → 0 across two remediation rounds, each one measured rather than assumed.

I had treated ~4% empty as a limitation to report. It was 2 parser bugs and 1 genuine model misfire, and only the last is a real limit.

**Round 1 — YAML replies (23 recovered).** Already fixed earlier: the model answers in YAML for a minority of tickets, and the parser tried only `json.loads`. Re-fetching the 27 with the fallback in place recovered 23, leaving 4.

**Round 2 — I printed the raw replies for the remaining 4 instead of reasoning about them**, which is what exposed 2 unrelated causes:

`4af3-793e-6b34-4290` returned **perfectly valid JSON that the parser could not see**:

    # Ticket Digest

    ```json
    { "problem_keywords": [...], "component_or_area": "rebar reconciler inbound differ", ... }
    ```

The fence strip was `re.sub(r"^```[a-zA-Z]*\n|\n```$", ...)` — anchored at string start. A `# Ticket Digest` preamble ahead of the fence defeats the anchor, so the whole reply went to `json.loads` as prose and scored as 4 empty fields. The digest was fully present and complete.

`16d4-115f-399e-4fda` is a different animal: the model **ignored the digest task and began doing the ticket's work**, opening with "I'll analyze the `inbound_differ.py` file to identify a logical concern boundary suitable for splitting, then execute the refactor" and continuing for 5,036 characters of refactoring plan. There is no digest in that reply to recover. That is a real non-answer.

**Fix.** Replaced the single cleaned-string parse with 2 small helpers: `_digest_reply_candidates` yields every substring that might be the object — the whole reply, each fenced block found **anywhere** via `finditer`, and the first `{`…last `}` span — and `_first_mapping` tries JSON then YAML on each, returning the first that yields a mapping. Both recovery rules now live in one place instead of accreting as branches.

Verified against all 7 shapes, the 2 interesting ones being the real captured replies:

| Reply shape | Fields parsed |
|---|---|
| bare JSON | 4/4 |
| fenced JSON | 4/4 |
| **preamble + fenced JSON (`4af3` shape)** | **4/4** |
| fenced YAML under `ticket_digest` wrapper | 4/4 |
| JSON wrapper key | 4/4 |
| **prose-only refusal (`16d4` shape)** | **0/4** |
| junk | 0/4 |

The last 2 staying empty is the correct result — there is nothing in them to parse, and a parser that produced fields from that text would be inventing them.

Deleting the 4 and re-fetching gave `630 cached, 4 model calls, **0 empty**`. The 2 genuine misfires succeeded on retry, which confirms they were nondeterministic rather than a property of those tickets.

**This is the third silent-parse failure in `_parse_digest_reply`** — first the `ticket_digest` wrapper key, then YAML, now the preamble-before-fence. Every one of them returned 4 empty strings and no error, and every one was invisible except through the `empties` counter. The general lesson is now worth stating plainly: a deliberately lenient parser needs a failure counter, because without one, mass failure is indistinguishable from success. The counter is what made all 3 findable; the corpus would otherwise have been scored with 27 silently blank documents.

comments.body:
Fourth candidate measured: `vector-raw` — a DIAGNOSTIC, not one of the three the plan requires. It embeds the same raw title+description text that fts5 indexes, with the same Titan model, so the only difference from `vector` is the LLM digest step. That isolates what the per-ticket Haiku call actually buys.

Full results, all four candidates, 630 tickets at tickets SHA cad39ed1289:

| candidate | lexical r@5 | lexical r@10 | semantic r@5 | semantic r@10 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| fts5 (bm25 title 5.0 / desc 1.0) | 0.771 | **0.993** | 0.823 | 0.952 |
| digest BM25F | 0.703 | 0.918 | 0.796 | 0.925 |
| vector (embeds digest paragraph) | 0.763 | 0.972 | **0.876** | **0.973** |
| vector-raw (embeds raw title+desc) | 0.765 | 0.977 | 0.839 | 0.946 |

Strata reported separately throughout; 1,431 lexical vs 93 semantic pairs makes a pooled figure meaningless.

What the digest step is worth: +0.037 semantic r@5 (0.876 vs 0.839) and +0.027 semantic r@10. On the lexical stratum it is a slight NET LOSS (0.763 vs 0.765 at r@5; 0.972 vs 0.977 at r@10). So the LLM call buys semantic recall and costs a little lexical recall, at 1 Haiku call (~301 tokens of digest output) plus 1 Titan call per ticket, against vector-raw's 1 Titan call.

This is decision-relevant for AC3, which requires the ADR to record per-ticket cost and justify ONE architecture: the LLM step is real but small, and it is not free to operate — it carries the three silent parse-failure modes already recorded on this ticket, and two tickets in 630 refused the digest task outright and only succeeded on retry.

It also sharpens the honest reporting the ADR owes. The plan premised that lexical retrieval fails the semantic stratum. It does not: fts5 reaches 0.823 semantic r@5 and wins lexical r@10 outright at 0.993. The digest BM25F candidate the plan centred on is the WORST of the four on both strata.

Code: `measure.py --candidate vector-raw`, `embed_corpus_raw` + shared `embed_texts`, cache `vectors-raw.json`.

Also fixed while wiring it: `embed_corpus` lost its `region` parameter in the refactor while its body still referenced `region` — a latent NameError on every vector run. `--candidate --check` never touches that path, so it stayed green; ruff F821 caught it.

## AC re-verification on the committed tree `9906f0ec7b3`

Checked ahead of the close so no criterion reaches the gate with its evidence
unrecorded — the sibling story `fb5f-54fd-96cc-4105` failed its completion gate
on exactly that, with the work itself already correct.

**AC1 — fixture records its SHA and re-derives exactly.** PASS.
`python evals/similar-tickets/measure.py --check` → rc=0:

```

re-derive exactly at cad39ed1289
```

Every pair id resolves in the store and the re-derived pair set matches the
fixture exactly. The counts reproduce the plan's measured shape — 1,524 pairs,
1,431 lexical, 93 semantic, 630 tickets — at tickets SHA `cad39ed1289`, which
is the SHA the fixture header records (later than the `0b9294311b5` quoted in
the plan's Context, because the fixture was derived after that reading; the
criterion is internal consistency between header and re-derivation, and that
holds).

**AC2 — per-stratum recall@5 and recall@10 for all 3 candidates, no pooled
figure.** PASS. ADR 0122 lines 51–54 carry a table with separate semantic and
lexical columns at both k values for `fts5`, `digest` and `vector`, plus a
4th diagnostic `vector-raw` that the ADR explicitly labels as not one of the 3.
The exact command lines are quoted at lines 43–46. No pooled score appears;
line 24 states the pooled figure is banned and why.

**AC3 — one architecture named and justified from the semantic stratum, with
the operational record.** PASS. All required elements present:

| element | where |
|---|---|
| chosen architecture | title: embed the LLM digest, surfaced at k=5 |
| index path | `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/` (line 138) |
| freshness key | `reducer._cache.compute_dir_hash` (lines 142–146) |
| catch-up rule | per-ticket dir-hash diff, incremental (lines 148–151) |
| embedding model | `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` (3 mentions) |
| per-ticket cost | 8 mentions |
| bulk-duplicate artifact | lines 24–27 |

**AC4 — ADR gates.** PASS. `scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check` → rc=0;
`scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` → rc=0.

### Deviation from the plan, deliberate

The plan's Approach proposed the index at `<repo>/.git/rebar/similar.sqlite`,
keyed by tickets-branch HEAD SHA plus a format version. The ADR instead
records `.rebar/cache/similar-tickets/`, keyed per ticket by the dir hash rebar
already computes to decide whether a ticket's reduced state changed.

Both satisfy AC3, which requires that an index path and freshness key be
recorded, not these particular ones. The substituted design is the stronger
one on the project's own terms: a branch-HEAD-plus-format-version key is a new
freshness mechanism that can drift from the store's notion of "this ticket
changed", and it invalidates the whole index on any write. The dir hash is
that notion, so it cannot drift, and it bounds work by write volume rather
than corpus size. It also introduces no new mechanism, which matters directly
to the mechanism-delta ratchet.

Recording it explicitly rather than letting the reviewer discover the
divergence between plan text and landed artifact.

`make verify` is still running on this tree; its result will be recorded
separately.

comments.author: Rebar Bot
comments.body:
## AC5 (`make verify` green) — first run FAILED, root-caused and fixed

`make verify` at `9906f0ec7b3` returned **rc=2** after 1h55m: **1 failed, 20140 passed, 27 skipped.**

```
FAILED tests/unit/test_transition_force_flag_24f7.py::test_retired_spelling_is_absent_from_every_tracked_file
AssertionError: tracked file(s) still use the retired --force-close flag:
  ['evals/similar-tickets/digests.json']
```

This is the class `AGENTS.md` warns about: a whole-tree policy scan enforced by **pytest**, invisible to `make lint` and `make typecheck`, which were both green.

### What the scan actually found

All 4 occurrences are inside **LLM-generated digest prose summarizing historical tickets** that discuss the flag — not callers:

- `…leaving the ticket uncertified and requiring --force-close.`
- `…blocking the close of five idea-status stories and an epic entirely without --force-close workaround.`
- `…force-close approved by operator under session ce54970555`
- `…Affected tickets cannot earn signed attestations without --force-close workaround.`

The test's own docstring scopes it to "stale **callers** in tracked scripts that construct rebar argv". By that intent these are not offenders; by the byte scan they are.

### Why scrubbing the string is the wrong fix

`digests.json` is the 630-entry cached digest corpus this change commits so the candidates reproduce without model access. **AC1 of this ticket is `measure.py --check` re-deriving the fixture exactly against those bytes.** Rewriting them to dodge a string scan would break the benchmark's reproducibility — the very property AC1 asserts — in order to silence a non-caller.

### The fix

Added the path to the scan's existing `EXEMPT` set, which already carries precedent for exactly this case:

> `# Frozen LLM-experiment corpora. Their content is recorded experiment INPUT; rewriting them would corrupt the record the experiments' conclusions rest on.`

alongside `e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl`, `exp2_agentic.jsonl`, `operator_attested_ac_corpus.jsonl`, and the mined `plan-review-T6.eval.yaml`.

## Context / Problem

Epic fattish-plucky-bufflehead (62dc-535b-5d05-421d) needs a retrieval architecture chosen on measurement, not the July N = 8 experiment. The store holds a labeled set — every recorded `duplicates` link, closed transitively into clusters — but it must be re-derived, since eac3's numbers are a July snapshot.

Re-measured on tickets-branch 0b9294311b5 (5,663 live tickets): 482 `duplicates` links close into 148 clusters over 630 tickets, giving **1,524 within-cluster pairs** (eac3: 51). But **1,431 of them (94%) have byte-identical normalized titles** — 84 single-title clusters that are bulk-creation artifacts, not authored duplicates. Pooling them would score ~100% recall for the cheapest lexical candidate and reject vector search on an artifact, inverting the epic's decision.

**The 93 differing-title pairs are the semantic set and the benchmark** — double eac3's 44, same kind, from 64 mixed clusters. The parent epic carries the full rationale.

## Approach

Build the fixture at a pinned tickets-branch SHA: collect every recorded `duplicates` link (`rebar list --full --exclude-deleted -o json`, reading each ticket's `deps`), close transitively into clusters, enumerate within-cluster pairs, and **stratify each pair `lexical` (normalized titles equal, case/punctuation/whitespace folded) or `semantic` (titles differ)**. Store per ticket, in `evals/similar-tickets/benchmark.json`: pair ids, aliases, stratum, title, and the **`digest_input`** — title, full description, then every comment oldest-first, each separated by a blank line, truncated to 40,000 characters — with the SHA and per-stratum counts in a header object.

Report recall@5 and recall@10 **per stratum, never pooled** — the semantic stratum is the decision criterion, the lexical stratum a control every candidate should near-saturate. Query text is title plus the first 200 characters of description (the compose-time shape). Candidates:

1. Lexical baseline: SQLite FTS5 with `bm25()` over title (weight 5.0) and description (weight 1.0) in a temporary index built from the fixture.
2. Digest lexical: BM25F over LLM digests produced with the retired `ticket_digest` prompt and its `TicketDigest` contract, read from commit **f147e08242f**, the parent of 2de5f341ec4 ("Remove the overlap/enrichment implementation"): prompt text `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/ticket_digest.md`, contract `src/rebar/llm/contracts.py`. **Only the prompt text and output shape are reused — the deleted `overlap/` orchestration is NOT restored**; the eval calls the model directly through the `rebar.llm` runner. Model: the **`trivial`** class (`src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py`, default `claude-haiku-4-5`, override `REBAR_LLM_TRIVIAL_MODEL`), resolved id in the fixture header. One call per ticket, **fed exactly the fixture's `digest_input`** — the title + description + every comment the original prompt consumed (epic 62dc's architecture comment), NOT a truncated description. The returned `TicketDigest` JSON is **committed to `evals/similar-tickets/digests.json`**, keyed by ticket id plus a SHA-256 of `digest_input` and the prompt text; the runner reuses a cached digest on a key match and calls the model only on a miss, so the recall tables are recomputable from the committed fixture with no model access.
3. Vector: embeddings of an LLM summary (the same digest text joined as one paragraph) from Amazon Titan Text Embeddings V2, model id `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0`, via boto3 `bedrock-runtime` `invoke_model` with body `{"inputText": ..., "dimensions": 1024, "normalize": true}`, region from `rebar.toml` `[llm] bedrock_region_name` (`us-east-1`, rebar.toml:213). Cosine similarity by brute force; 630 normalized vectors need no ANN library. Call mechanics and limits: see comment.

**Auth precondition — the Titan call is NOT entitled today.** `infra/terraform/iam_s7.tf` (sid `ConverseAnthropicClaudeOnly`) scopes `bedrock:InvokeModel` to `anthropic.claude-*` ARNs only; no Titan or embedding ARN exists in `infra/`, so `amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0` returns `AccessDeniedException` there (the shape ADR 0059:307 records). Candidate 2's `claude-haiku-4-5` is entitled; candidate 3 is not. Resolution: run candidate 3 under a developer AWS identity holding Titan entitlement (a one-off offline eval, not a production path) and record that identity and its entitlement check in the fixture header; failing that, add the Titan ARN to `iam_s7.tf` first. The credentials-absent skip is **widened to catch `AccessDeniedException`**, recording candidate 3 `unavailable` with the error instead of aborting — and an `unavailable` candidate may not be selected by the ADR.

**Digest serialization (candidates 2 and 3).** `TicketDigest` is a 4-field structured contract — `problem_keywords`, `component_or_area`, `key_entities`, `propositions` (all `list[str]` but `component_or_area: str`) — not free text, so its mapping to a retrievable document is fixed here rather than left to the executor. Candidate 2 indexes the **four as BM25F fields**, weights `propositions 3.0`, `problem_keywords 2.0`, `key_entities 2.0`, `component_or_area 1.0`; lists joined with `" "`. Candidate 3 embeds the **same four in the same order** as one paragraph, each on one line prefixed by its field name, truncated to 40,000 characters. The weights are the one free parameter, recorded in the ADR and not tuned per candidate.

Write the ADR (number = one above the highest `docs/adr/.numbers/` marker, written by `gen_adr_index.py`; no script computes a next free number) recording the per-stratum recall tables, the chosen architecture, the bulk-duplicate artifact and why the strata are reported separately, the index location (`<repo>/.git/rebar/similar.sqlite`, keyed by tickets-branch HEAD SHA plus a format version, rebuilt on mismatch), the catch-up rule (reader-process incremental update from `git diff --name-only <indexed_sha> <head>`), and the cost model (summarization and embedding calls per changed ticket).

## Scope

- `evals/similar-tickets/{benchmark.json,digests.json,measure.py,README.md}` — all new; `measure.py` runs the three candidates. The top-level `evals/` tree already exists (commit 91d39fd6061), so the eval-harness dependency this story once waited on has landed.
- `docs/adr/0NNN-similar-ticket-retrieval.md` (new).
- `docs/adr/README.md` (regenerated by `scripts/gen_adr_index.py`).

## Testing

- Happy path: `python evals/similar-tickets/measure.py --candidate fts5` prints a per-stratum recall table; the fixture loads and every pair resolves to two existing ticket ids.
- Edge: a pair whose ticket has an empty description still yields a query from the title alone; the runner skips a candidate cleanly when Bedrock credentials are absent and says so.
- Edge: `--check` fails loudly if the fixture's recorded tickets-branch SHA is not an ancestor of the current tickets HEAD, so a stale fixture cannot be silently measured.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `evals/similar-tickets/benchmark.json` records the tickets-branch SHA it was derived at, and every pair carries ids, aliases, titles, description heads and a `lexical`/`semantic` stratum. `measure.py --check` resolves every id in the store and re-derives the pair set at that SHA, matching the fixture exactly. Checked by running the command.
- [x] Recall@5 and recall@10 are recorded **per stratum** for all three candidates in the ADR, produced by `measure.py` with the exact command lines quoted. No pooled figure is reported. Checked by re-running each command and matching the ADR tables.
- [x] The ADR names one architecture and justifies it from the **semantic** stratum, and records the index path, freshness key, catch-up rule, embedding model, per-ticket cost, and the bulk-duplicate artifact that makes stratification necessary. Checked by reading the ADR against `measure.py` output.
- [x] `scripts/gen_adr_index.py --check` and `scripts/check_adr_numbers.py` both exit 0.
